The conditions say $\pi$ is an involution (since $\pi(\pi(i)) = i$ for all $i$) with no fixed points (since $\pi(i) \neq i$ for all $i$).

An involution splits $\{1,\dots,10\}$ into 2-cycles and fixed points. Having no fixed points means every element lies in a 2-cycle. Such a permutation is exactly a perfect matching of the 10 elements, where each pair $\{a,b\}$ is swapped by $\pi$. The map from perfect matchings to these permutations is a bijection.

The number of perfect matchings of $2n$ elements is $(2n-1)!! = (2n-1)(2n-3)\cdots 3\cdot 1$. For $2n = 10$:

$$9!! = 9 \cdot 7 \cdot 5 \cdot 3 \cdot 1 = 945.$$

As a check, choose the partner of element 1 in 9 ways. Then recursively match the remaining 8 elements, which gives $9 \cdot 7 \cdot 5 \cdot 3 \cdot 1 = 945$.

ANSWER: 945
